skill_traces.query:
Jon: Hey Gina, I had to shut down my bank account. It was tough, but I needed to do it for my biz.
Gina: Oh no, Jon! Sorry to hear that. Tough decision for you? How're you handling the changes?
Jon: It was a tough call, but I thought it'd help my biz grow. Handling changes has been hard, but I'm staying positive and looking ahead. Anything new for you?
Gina: Oof, that's tough, Jon. I got some new offers and promotions going on my online store to try and bring in new customers. It's been a wild ride starting my business, but I'm not giving up!
Jon: Nice one, Gina! Love how you never give up. What helps you stay motivated?
Gina: Thanks Jon! Dance is my stress relief and fashion fuels my creativity. I love finding new trends for my store. It keeps me motivated to keep growing. Check out this pic of my fave dance session!
Jon: Wow, that's great! What made you combine clothing biz and dance?
Gina: Thanks! I'm passionate about dance and fashion so combining them lets me show my creativity and share my love with others. Plus, I can add dance-inspired items to my store!
Jon: Nice work! Combining passions is always cool. How's it going?
Gina: Thanks! So far, so good - customers love the new offers and promotions, which means I'm seeing more sales. People seem to really like my designs, so I'm always on the hunt for unique, trendy pieces. Growing my customer base is the main focus right now.
Jon: Sounds like all your effort's paying off. Anything planned to grow your customer base?
Gina: Yeah, I have a few plans. I'm thinking of working with some fashion bloggers and influencers in the next few months to get more attention for my store. Plus, I'm going to do more ads so I can reach more people. I'm really focused on building my customer base and making my store a top destination for fashion fans. It's awesome to see it all coming together! You, Jon? What do you have going for your dance studio?
Jon: Thanks, Gina! I'm expanding my dance studio's social media presence and offering workshops and classes to local schools and centers. I'm also hosting a dance competition next month to showcase local talent and bring more attention to my studio. All the work's paying off - I'm seeing progress and the dancers are so excited. It's such a great feeling to give a place where people can express themselves through dance!
Gina: Wow! That's fantastic that your studio's expanding and giving dancers an outlet. So proud of the progress you've made - keep it up!
Jon: Thanks! Your backing means a lot. I'm trying to make my plan work, even though it's been tough. Your encouragement really helps. Are you coming to the event next month? Love to have you there!
Gina: Woah, cool event! What's gonna be happening? I'd love to join in and show my support!
Jon: Thanks, Gina! My dance studio and some other schools are bringing their best moves for an awesome night of performances and judging. It'll be super creative and fun. Come join us!
Gina: Sounds great! I'm definitely in for the show.
Jon: Cool! Can't wait to see you!
Gina: Thanks, Jon! See you at the event!
Jon: Gina, good luck with your store!
Gina: Thanks, Jon! Appreciate the kind words. <3
Jon: Sure, I am always there for you!
Gina: Thanks! Your support means a lot. I'm gonna keep pursuing my goals and I hope you do too!
Jon: Thanks! I won't quit on my dreams. Your words really motivate me. Bye!
Gina: Bye Jon! You got this! Believe in yourself and keep pushing. Take care!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Facts from Photo or Keepsake Statements

content: Treat statements about photos, albums, videos, or keepsakes as potential carriers of facts.

Extract only facts explicitly stated; do not infer.
